$comment: Machine-readable inventory of the Mission-Bound Authorization family's draft-*.md files at repo root (see the `count` field below for the current total). Single source of truth for DRAFTS.md's generated catalog index, the architecture document map, each draft's role, spec maturity, verb, summary, adoption trigger, and typed reference and adoption edges; reference_stacks transcribes the architecture document's OAuth reference stacks. Validate with scripts/check-family-manifest.mjs.
generated_note: Hand-curated; re-derive `role`, `spec_maturity`, and `group` from each draft's front matter and Status section when drafts are added, renamed, or reclassified. `role` (core, adapter-binding, companion, or guide) is architectural: core is the binding-neutral substrate kernel; adapter-binding is any draft publishing a Mission Substrate Statement or Assessment capability table (scripts/check-substrate-statements.mjs's REGISTRY); guide is every category:info document; companion is everything else. `spec_maturity` (candidate, experimental, sketch, or not_applicable) is a five-criteria gate resolved against structured evidence in candidate-gate.json (scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs's validateCandidateGate()), not a raw coverage percentage and not inferred from a Conformance heading: an attested, commit-verified complete requirement inventory for the claimed interface; no open decide issue scoped to that interface without a recorded resolved_in_tree resolution; a named interoperability/conformance floor; examples/vectors or a recorded waiver; disclosed unstable external normative dependencies. `category` (front matter's std/exp/info) is the document's intended standards category (requested RFC category, never WG adoption, approval, or publication state) and needs no separate axis. Implementation/conformance coverage is derived from conformance-manifest.json per spec at generation time (scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs's family-status block) and is never hand-written here. `verbs`, `summary`, and `pull_when` are authorial here: `verbs` draws on the architecture document's verb spine, and DRAFTS.md's index block is generated from these fields by scripts/generate-drafts-index.mjs and validated against them, not the other way round. `requires` is re-derived from each draft's front-matter normative references (drift-checked in CI), `references` from its full in-family reference set, and `reference_stacks` transcribes the architecture document's four cumulative stacks.
known_non_family_refs: draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture.md's Mission Document Map also names oauth-id-continuation-assertion. That is an adjacent, non-family draft (no draft-*.md file in this repo) and is intentionally absent from drafts[] below; do not add a phantom manifest entry for it.

reference_stacks.$comment: A transcription of the Architecture's four cumulative reference stacks ({#reference-architecture} in draft-mcguinness-mission-architecture) in their OAuth realization: the Architecture itself frames the protocol core as 'the OAuth realization of Baseline Issuance' and the reference stack as presuming an authority-bearing binding, so these stacks pin the OAuth binding and the binding decision stays separate (the README's binding table). Other bindings realize the levels per their own documents: standalone MAS has no issuance gate unless the Issuance Grant is composed; AAuth reports native capabilities rather than claiming the levels, and the Person Server's contextual gate is its per-action analogue on PS-mediated paths; UMA and GNAP are experimental sketches. The Architecture is authoritative and this object must change only when {#reference-architecture} does; each stack's architecture_name is tripwired against that document's text in CI. `freshness_one_of`: the Runtime-Enforced level requires one freshness source; a `core:` entry names a facility of the binding rather than a separate document. Adoption closure beyond a stack follows each draft's `adoption_requires` edges. One recorded reading: `adds` includes draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence, which {#reference-architecture}'s three-item sentence omits but the Document Map groups under runtime enforcement and the Runtime-Enforced level's evidence obligation presumes. Provisional until v0 proper passes its publication gate. The OAuth pin is an infrastructure choice, never a maturity ranking: no production Mission deployment is known today, and Missions on OAuth still require the changes the OAuth binding defines.

protocol-core.summary: The OAuth issuance profile alone: approved, anchored, state-gated Missions with no per-action control.

reference-security-architecture.summary: The default evaluation shape: point-of-use permits with durable decision and execution evidence, plus a freshness source.

recommended-agent-architecture.summary: What a deployment running autonomous AI agents should build: session-continuity stop and proof of what the Approver saw.

high-assurance-architecture.summary: The recommended architecture plus the named per-path claims; a claims level, not an additional document list.

drafts.title: AAuth Mission Expiry
drafts.summary: Profiles AAuth's `expires_at` mission-blob member: an immutable, consent-bound lifetime the base protocol enforces on every Person Server decision path, with lifetime caps on every token carrying `mission_s256`.
drafts.pull_when: A citable profile of AAuth's native `expires_at` is needed (base AAuth enforces it regardless; the profile's own conformance line is OPTIONAL).

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Authorization for the Agent Access Model
drafts.summary: Maps Cloudflare's Agent Access Model onto the family, realizing each of its six components with an existing mechanism and declining the grant review loop because Missions are not standing grants.
drafts.pull_when: Adopting Cloudflare's AAM vocabulary and mapping it onto existing mechanisms.

drafts.title: Mission Context Binding for AAuth
drafts.summary: The thin AAuth-native binding: it uses AAuth's existing mission blob, `{approver, s256}` reference, propose/clarify/approve flow, and active and terminated states unchanged, and defines no new wire members.
drafts.pull_when: The substrate is AAuth: Mission context on its native propose/approve flow.
drafts.maintenance_exception: 2026-08-20 (#554, PR #621): the Mission Substrate Statement migration to the supplied/not-supplied format is a substrate-contract conformance change applied under owner direction; no AAuth wire member or protocol behavior changed. The frozen-until-upstream-release text-fix policy is otherwise unchanged.

drafts.title: AAuth Mission Management
drafts.summary: The AAuth-native companion promised by the AAuth protocol: authenticated status, permanent termination, optional immutable expiry, and delegation-tree queries at the Person Server `mission_control_endpoint`.
drafts.pull_when: Alongside the AAuth binding: status, termination, delegation-tree queries.

drafts.title: Mission Approval Governance
drafts.summary: Extracts approval-authority provenance into the Approval Governance Record: an issuer-retained, issuer-signed record of who approved, under which authority, and why the decision satisfied governance.
drafts.pull_when: Approval authority itself needs authenticated, policy-backed provenance.

requires_when.when: the Approval Context Manifest is computed for a Mission whose record carries a Progressive ceiling

drafts.title: An Architecture for Mission-Bound Authorization
drafts.summary: The single structural view: the delegated-authority-layer thesis, a Mission's life end to end, the seven invariants, the substrate interface, the verb spine, the Mission Assurance Levels, and the Deployment Profile.
drafts.pull_when: Before adopting anything: the Mission model, invariants, and assurance levels the rest cite.

drafts.title: Mission Audit Transparency
drafts.summary: Makes the suite's evidence tamper-evident and independently verifiable by registering it into a SCITT Transparency Service as Signed Statements.
drafts.pull_when: A cross-domain party must verify evidence integrity without trusting issuer logs.

requires_when.when: approval governance records are audited
discovery evidence is audited
harness or egress evidence is audited
the Mandate profile is deployed
runtime decision or execution evidence is audited
child delegation evidence is audited
consent evidence is audited
containment evidence is audited
lifecycle transitions arrive as Signals
work-product bindings are audited

drafts.title: Mission Authority Server
drafts.summary: A peer binding, the AS-optional deployment mode, and the estate control plane of the delegated-authority layer.
drafts.pull_when: The AS cannot change: run Mission governance as a standalone control plane.

requires_when.when: an approval-governance recording trigger holds
runtime enforcement covers consequential paths
the AuthZEN binding emits Decision Evidence
the Expansion and Child Creation capability is claimed

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Runtime Enforcement: AuthZEN Profile
drafts.summary: The concrete OpenID AuthZEN binding of the runtime decision contract.
drafts.pull_when: The PDP speaks AuthZEN and needs the decision-contract wire mapping.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate
cross-domain projected credentials are evaluated
Status supplies state and the Effective Authority Set
the deployment claims the Runtime Evidence feature profile, rather than the Decision Base alone

drafts.title: Mission Capability Binding
drafts.summary: Binds a Mission's approved catalog-sourced entry (an MCP tool, an OpenAPI operation, or an equivalent) to the capability source it was derived from: `tool_id`, source, and a content digest recorded at derivation and verified at decision time.
drafts.pull_when: Actions come from a discovered catalog where invoked identity can drift from approval.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate

drafts.title: Mission Open-World Discovery
drafts.summary: Makes discovery a governed operation for agents that meet resources their approval could not name, defining the Encounter, resource identity pinning, two-mode Discovery Adjudication, and Discovery Evidence.
drafts.pull_when: An open-world agent meets resources its approval never named.

requires_when.when: the harness supplies taint state
ceiling adjudication is the deployed mode

drafts.title: Mission Evidence Envelope
drafts.summary: A generic, binding-neutral evidence envelope and payload-type registry a future evidence kind MAY register into instead of minting a one-off object and media type, seeded with Intent Admission Evidence as its first payload type; migrates none of the family's existing evidence kinds.
drafts.pull_when: A new evidence kind is being designed and a deployment wants to avoid minting another bespoke media type, or Intent Admission Evidence's inbound assertion and emitted attestation are needed.

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Authorization for GNAP
drafts.summary: Experimental sketch: the fifth binding, to the Grant Negotiation and Authorization Protocol (RFC 9635) authorization server, and the second authored against the Mission Substrate Requirements contract.
drafts.pull_when: Evaluating a GNAP deployment only.

requires_when.when: grant modification creates an Expansion successor
Mission Containment is adopted
the Status profile is adopted

drafts.title: Mission-Aware Agent Harnesses
drafts.summary: How an agent harness binds sessions, task graphs, queues, and sub-agent handles to Mission state, and how it must pause, suppress, or terminate work once the Mission is no longer active.
drafts.pull_when: A harness holds session state across restarts and must stop work when the Mission dies.

requires_when.when: a gateway PEP outside the harness carries the Mission reference
the OAuth binding is the substrate
Status is the freshness source

drafts.title: Mission Mandate
drafts.summary: A signed, portable, independently verifiable statement of a Mission's committed facts (its identifiers, integrity anchors, Subject, Approver, and optionally its Authority Set), minted by the Mission Issuer.
drafts.pull_when: An outside party must verify what was approved without a token-exchange hop.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate

drafts.title: Mission Consumption Metering
drafts.summary: Defines the cumulative consumption bounds a Mission Intent may carry (`max_budget`, `max_calls`, `max_duration`, `max_egress_volume`), the `exclusive` latch, and the runtime metering and AuthZEN wire binding that enforce them.
drafts.pull_when: A Mission needs cumulative caps (budget, calls, duration, egress), not just scope.

requires_when.when: the AuthZEN binding is the runtime wire
Consent Evidence is recorded

drafts.title: Mission Orchestration and Unwinding
drafts.summary: How a multi-step or multi-Mission workflow assigns a reversibility class to each step, records an unwind plan before dispatch, and unwinds in-flight work safely when a Mission stops.
drafts.pull_when: In-flight work must unwind safely if the Mission ends mid-workflow.

requires_when.when: the harness profile is co-deployed
compensation links runtime evidence
the OAuth binding is the substrate
Status polling is the trigger source
Signals is the authority-change trigger source

drafts.title: Mission Runtime Evidence
drafts.summary: The binding-neutral Decision Evidence, Execution Evidence, and Refusal Record objects a decision-API binding's PDP and PEP emit: their members, canonicalization, integrity envelope, media types, and retention.
drafts.pull_when: Runtime enforcement is deployed and decisions need durable, verifiable records.

requires_when.when: cross-domain projected decisions are recorded

drafts.title: Mission Runtime OAuth Adapter
drafts.summary: The OAuth 2.0 realization of the runtime core's binding-neutral contract: token presentation and validation, the `mission`/`act`/`cnf`/`aud` claim mapping, the `authorization_details` and `mission_resource_access` authority-entry mapping, and Resource-Owner Class Floors through OAuth protected resource metadata.
drafts.pull_when: The Mission-bound credential is an OAuth access token and the runtime core's abstract roles need their concrete OAuth realization.

requires_when.when: the deployment maps a mission_resource_access authorization_details entry

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Runtime Enforcement
drafts.summary: A binding-neutral decision contract for enforcing a Mission-bound credential at the point of use: within a declared enforcement scope, before each consequential action a Policy Enforcement Point obtains a permit from a Policy Decision Point that evaluates the action against the Mission.
drafts.pull_when: Actions need a point-of-use check, not just issuance-time gating.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate

drafts.title: Mission Transaction Authorization Profile for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Profiles the OAuth transaction authorization challenge for the Mission cross-domain case: a Transaction Authorization Server runs a fresh decision with a governed approval as input and issues a sender-constrained, single-use transaction token the resource verifies offline.
drafts.pull_when: One action needs a fresh, portable, cross-org authorization with no live callback.

drafts.title: Mission Security Model
drafts.summary: A cross-cutting, Informational consolidation of the suite's trusted base.
drafts.pull_when: Reviewing or auditing: the one consolidated trust and blast-radius view.

drafts.title: Mission Intent Shaping
drafts.summary: How a client-side "shaper" turns a user's request into a candidate Mission Intent before it is submitted.
drafts.pull_when: You need a defined client-side path from user prompt to candidate Mission Intent.

requires_when.when: shaping evidence digests are produced
the OAuth binding is the substrate

drafts.title: Mission Substrate Requirements
drafts.summary: For authors of new bindings: a small, normative contextual-governance kernel (native Mission reference, identified Controller, authenticated Actor binding, immutable Approved Context, approval event, active/non-active gate, context propagation, ordered governance record), with stronger properties declared separately as capabilities.
drafts.pull_when: Runtime implementers consume its commitment construction and kernel contract; binding authors profile it.

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Authorization for UMA 2.0
drafts.summary: Experimental sketch: the fourth binding, and the first authored against the Mission Substrate Requirements contract rather than extracted into it.
drafts.pull_when: Evaluating a UMA 2.0 deployment only.

drafts.title: Mission Approval Revision for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Adds a `revisable` mode to Deferred Approval: the Authorization Server signals which dimensions it refused and invites the client to push a narrowing revision, continuing the same deferred approval instead of starting over.
drafts.pull_when: Reviewers routinely narrow a proposed Mission rather than approve or deny.

drafts.title: Mission Deferred Approval for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Makes the approval event asynchronous, profiling OAuth Deferred Token Response so a Mission approval can be deferred and polled.
drafts.pull_when: Approval is asynchronous: a human review queue, not an immediate decision.

requires_when.when: an Approval Governance Record is recorded

drafts.title: Mission Offline Attenuation for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Removes the Authorization Server from the sub-agent fan-out hot path, profiling Attenuating Agent Tokens so a Mission-bound token holder mints a narrower child token offline.
drafts.pull_when: Deep fan-out makes an AS round-trip per narrowing too costly; mint offline.

drafts.title: Mission Child Delegation for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Lets a parent Mission authorize a Child Mission for a sub-agent, with explicit parent lineage, strict-subset authority, expiry no later than the parent, fan-out controls, and cascade revocation when the parent reaches a terminal state.
drafts.pull_when: A sub-agent needs its own Mission outliving a call frame, with cascade termination.

requires_when.when: cascade revocation reacts to parent lifecycle states
the deployment also runs the Entry Discharge companion

drafts.title: Mission Consent Evidence for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Commits the structured consent disclosure shown to the Approver at the approval event, through a `consent_rendering_hash` and a signed Consent Evidence object, so an auditor can reconstruct the recorded approval surface.
drafts.pull_when: You must prove what the Approver actually saw, not only what was approved.

requires_when.when: an Approval Governance Record is recorded

drafts.title: Mission Containment for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Narrows a live Mission without ending it: on a declared protected event the Mission Issuer commits a contain transition whose issuer-held, monotonic, removal-only overlay gates every derivation while the approved anchors stay immutable.
drafts.pull_when: A live Mission must be narrowed, not ended, on a protected event.

requires_when.when: contained authority is restored via a successor

drafts.title: Mission Continuation: Authorization Continuity for Mission-Bound Authorization
drafts.summary: Profiles authorization continuity: how a Mission's work continues across hops and over time without re-presenting the original credential and without widening authority.
drafts.pull_when: Authorized work continues across hops or time without re-presented credentials.

requires_when.when: the async-delegation transport creates refresh families

drafts.title: Mission Cross-Domain Projection for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Lets a single Mission be honored by Authorization Servers in other trust domains: the originating issuer projects audience-scoped authority through a short-lived, sender-constrained cross-domain grant, and the Resource AS mints its own local Mission-bound tokens preserving the `mission` claim.
drafts.pull_when: A Mission from one trust domain must be honored by an AS in another (also the floor's conditional dependency).

drafts.title: Mission Cross-Organizational Delegation for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Profiles Mission Offline Attenuation across organizational trust domains: an agent in one organization delegates a narrowed slice to an agent in another, and the relying party verifies the complete narrowing chain without calling the origin on the request path.
drafts.pull_when: An attenuation chain crosses organizational trust domains.

requires_when.when: a local token is minted from a verified Chain

drafts.title: Mission Completion and Entry Discharge for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Registers `terminal_when`, an OPTIONAL Common Constraint naming one or more entry-grain completion conditions, and the authenticated `discharge` operation, registered as an extension on the Status profile's Mission Lifecycle endpoint, that commits a condition's firing and retires the entry's authority without ending the Mission.
drafts.pull_when: One Authority Set entry's task finishes before the rest of the Mission, and its authority should retire itself rather than wait for a Mission-level revoke, expiry, or complete.

drafts.title: Mission Expansion for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: How to widen a Mission's authority: because authority can only narrow within a Mission, widening requires a fresh approval that creates a successor Mission superseding its predecessor.
drafts.pull_when: Approved authority will predictably need to widen mid-task via fresh approval.

drafts.title: Mission Issuance Grant for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: The issuance join: the middle integration between the standalone binding and a natively Mission-aware AS.
drafts.pull_when: A MAS-governed estate wants Mission-bound gated tokens without full intake at each AS.

requires_when.when: Status supplies state and the Effective Authority Set

drafts.title: Mission Management for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: The fleet-management surface the status profile defers: authenticated Mission enumeration and bulk lifecycle operations, dry-run first, with a per-Mission outcome manifest.
drafts.pull_when: An operator needs fleet enumeration and bulk lifecycle across many Missions.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate
the standalone MAS is the binding
Child Mission lineage filters are used

drafts.title: Mission Progressive Authorization for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: At the initial approval the Approver also consents to an authority ceiling and a drawdown policy, letting the Mission Issuer adjudicate an in-ceiling expansion by policy instead of a fresh human approval.
drafts.pull_when: Authority cannot be enumerated up front; policy-bounded drawdown beats over-provisioning.

requires_when.when: drawdown maps to the runtime profile's action classes

drafts.title: Mission Resource Access Profile for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Defines mission_resource_access, split from the OAuth binding: resource exact/prefix matching, the action namespace and wildcard families, Common Constraints, per-entry delegation policy, and the subset/intersection algebra, plus this type's scope-projection safety conditions and machine-readable transformation-capability declaration.
drafts.pull_when: The OAuth binding's supported authorization_details types include mission_resource_access, or you need its concrete subset/delegation/projection semantics.

drafts.title: Mission Lifecycle Signals for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: A profile of the OpenID Shared Signals Framework: the Mission Issuer emits a signed Security Event Token on each Mission lifecycle transition, delivered by push or poll, so a consumer learns of a transition promptly without polling.
drafts.pull_when: Consumers need push notice of state changes instead of polling per Mission.

requires_when.when: the OAuth binding is the substrate
the deployment also runs the Entry Discharge companion

drafts.title: Mission Status and Lifecycle for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: A `mission_id`-keyed status surface with signed responses, plus a lifecycle endpoint for explicit `revoke`, `suspend`, `resume`, and `complete` transitions and the `suspended` and `completed` states.
drafts.pull_when: You must observe or change Mission state beyond token expiry (revoke, suspend, complete).

drafts.title: Mission Status List for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: Profiles a Mission Status List, a signed, compressed OAuth Status List bit array a consumer relying on many Missions at once fetches once per freshness window and reads locally per action, as a `status_list` extension member on the Status profile's response and introspection surfaces.
drafts.pull_when: A consumer relies on many Missions concurrently and per-Mission status reads do not scale.

drafts.title: Mission Template for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: An Approver consents once to a task template (a ceiling of resources, actions, and constraints plus a dispatch policy), and each dispatch then instantiates an ordinary, independently gated Mission from it at machine speed.
drafts.pull_when: Machine-speed dispatch makes per-run approval infeasible; consent once to a ceiling.

drafts.title: Mission Work Products
drafts.summary: Keeps information from carrying authority: a policy-free work-product provenance object attributes an artifact to the approved work that produced it, and a non-transitive handoff rule makes the receiving Mission re-evaluate any proposed action under its own Authority Set.
drafts.pull_when: Artifacts cross into another Mission and must carry provenance, never authority.

drafts.title: Mission-Bound Authorization for OAuth 2.0
drafts.summary: The OAuth 2.0 binding of the Mission model, the issuance profile to its OAuth companions: defines the OAuth realization of the Mission, the Mission Intent and Authority Set, the approval event and its `intent_hash` / `authority_hash` anchors, the `mission` token claim, the subset rule, and state-gated issuance.
drafts.pull_when: Start here for OAuth issuance: any agent's approval must bind durably to the tokens it later uses.
